newsitem.title: POLAND: THREE FOREIGN FIRMS BID FOR POLISH DRUG FIRM - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: THREE FOREIGN FIRMS BID FOR POLISH DRUG FIRM - PAPER.

text.p: Poland's treasury ministry has shorlisted three large foreign companies in a tender for at least 10 percent of the state-owned drug maker Polfa Poznan SA, the Rzeczpospolita daily reported on Tuesday.
The paper, quoting an anonymous source close to the tender, said the shorlist included the Norwegian group Nycomed ASA, Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc and U.S. Bristol Myers Squibb Co.
The treasury ministry's press office declined to confirm the report.
The Rzepospolita paper said the investors were ready the pay between $150 million and $250 million for a majority stake in Polfa Poznan.
The paper said the three companies had until the end of August to submit final offers.

Polfa Poznan's spokesman Przemyslaw Nowicki also declined to comment on the report, saying only that his company was in talks with foreign firms on the privatisation. He said the privatisation should be completed by the end of the year.
Polfa Poznan, based in the western city of Poznan, netted about 60 million zlotys last year on sales of about 284 million zlotys. Nowicki said the net profit was likely to improve in 1997.
